clue.text: Astounded doctor mocked bags

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed that a physician has made fun of some luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as a noun, the one doing the mocking, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange MOCKED BAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang synonym: utterly amazed, as if struck in the mouth.

clue.text: In the morning European follows good sport

indicators.note: the morning and European letters come after the letter for good

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: In the morning a European comes along after some good sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest played by rules, such as football, is a match or form of sport.

clue.text: Group outlawed on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so one word stands for another that sounds the same

parts.note: outlawed means banned, prohibited

explanation.surface: A pop group has been banned from radio play.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical ensemble, or any company of people, is a group.

clue.text: Roam semi-nude somehow causing offence

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Wandering around half-dressed leads to trouble with the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor crime or wrongdoing is an offence, less serious than a felony.

clue.text: Leaders of choral association regularly oversee lyrics in song

indicators.note: the leaders of the five words that follow are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Heads of a choir society routinely check the words of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but it is just one of the five words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive hymn, sung especially at Christmas, is a kind of song.

clue.text: Suitable old exercise regimen involving bit of netting

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: the diet takes in the letter from netting

parts.note: a diet is a regimen of eating

indicators.note: a bit of the word netting is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fitting description of an outdated workout plan that includes some netting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something convenient and practical for a purpose, if not principled, is suitable.

clue.text: Fleece coats returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for coats is read backwards

parts.note: macs are raincoats, short for mackintoshes

explanation.surface: A sheep's wool covering coats that have come back from the cleaners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like a noun about wool or a jacket, but here it is the verb to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to cheat them out of money, which is exactly a con or swindle.

clue.text: Gossip article few chat luridly about

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the article
told luridly, the words are lurched into a wild new order

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A tabloid piece where a little sensational chatter goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts THE inside CHEWFAT, the anagram of FEW CHAT signalled by 'luridly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for chatting idly at length, which is to gossip.

clue.text: Endless complaint appropriate journalist modified incorrectly

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a malady is an illness or complaint
apt means appropriate
ED is short for editor, a senior journalist

explanation.surface: A never-ending grievance about a fitting reporter who was wrongly changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Poorly suited to an environment, having been altered or evolved badly, is this adjective.

clue.text: Manchester United's epitaph in court document

parts.note: Man U is the common short name for Manchester United football club, plus S for the possessive

indicators.note: the epitaph sits inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the classic epitaph on a gravestone

explanation.surface: A football club's farewell words read out in a legal setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A handwritten or typed original text, especially before printing, is a kind of document.

clue.text: Loudly auction off part of prison

indicators.note: said out loud, one word is heard as another that is spelt differently

parts.note: to auction off goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Someone noisily selling off a section of a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner's small locked room is one unit within a jail.

clue.text: Dodgy challenge to get fit

parts.note: to question a claim is to challenge it
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: A shady challenge to get into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Of doubtful honesty or soundness, that is suspicious, is a sense of dodgy.

clue.text: Balanced spa advertisement exactly on centre of aqueduct

parts.note: a spa town is built on a mineral spring, also called a well
an ad is short for an advertisement
just means exactly, as in 'just so'

indicators.note: the centre of the eight-letter word aqueduct is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A notice for a spa sitting right on top of the middle of a water bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychologically stable, emotionally steady person is described as having a balanced mind.

clue.text: Are not in use, seemingly

indicators.note: the contraction sits inside the verb for use

parts.note: to apply something is to use it
aren't is the contraction of are not

explanation.surface: Things that look as if they are idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean as far as one can tell, judging by appearances.

clue.text: Writings hacked by alternative lawyer

parts.note: prose is ordinary written work
hacked means cut
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone's writings have been broken into by an alternative attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: The lawyer who brings a criminal case against an accused person in court.

clue.text: Carry on to each extreme

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'ten pounds per person'
severe means extreme, as in severe weather

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep going all the way to either end.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep at something despite difficulty is to carry on, a synonym.

clue.text: Get rid of unusual alien item

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters is a different order

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispose of a strange extraterrestrial object.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove or do away with completely is to get rid of.

clue.text: Woman starts to embrace pet ruminant

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words give their first letters

explanation.surface: A woman begins to hug her pet, a cud-chewing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruminant is a cud-chewing mammal, and this woolly farm animal is one example.

clue.text: Clergyman loses head for crime

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar is beheaded for some wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Complex about being surrounded by popular and banal

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular, as in 'the in thing'

indicators.note: the word for about sits inside the word for banal

parts.note: trite means banal, overused
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A complicated idea about being surrounded by things popular yet dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with many detailed, interwoven parts is complex; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Crashing exciting car across middle of mound is very painful

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stretch across the middle letter, holding it inside
a crashing car is wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order
the middle of the five-letter word mound is its third letter

explanation.surface: An exciting car crashing over a hump is an agonising experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts U (the middle of 'mound') inside EXCRCIATING, the anagram of EXCITING CAR made by 'Crashing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means agonising, intensely painful, from the Latin for torture on a cross.

clue.text: Time to defeat swimmer

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: It is time to beat a rival in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' suggests a human athlete but is a crossword way of saying fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish is something that swims, a crossword-only sense of swimmer.

clue.text: Secure silver in church

indicators.note: the silver symbol is placed within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Lock up the silverware in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine, as a bird behind bars, is to secure it.

clue.text: Upended garden feature over time becomes liability

indicators.note: in a down entry the turned word sits over, above, the time letter
upended in a down entry means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a flower bed is a garden feature

explanation.surface: A garden bed turned over eventually becomes a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed is a financial liability.

clue.text: Small drinks small child returns

indicators.note: returning means the letters for small and child are read backwards

parts.note: S is the usual clothing abbreviation for small
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A little child comes back with some modest drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Small measures of spirits such as whisky are called by this name, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Unruly Labrador swallowing unknown electronic grooming device

indicators.note: the rearranged dog takes the unknown letter inside it
an unruly dog is out of order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Z is one of the algebra letters used for an unknown quantity
E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A badly behaved dog gulps down a mysterious electronic gadget used for grooming.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaving tool is a device used in personal grooming.

clue.text: Lose energy in long story

indicators.note: to lose a letter is to take it away from the word

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn for it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop being energetic during a lengthy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long story' looks like one phrase, the definition, but 'long' belongs to the wordplay as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale, especially a rambling or tall one, is a synonym.

clue.text: Colony arrangement

definitions.meaning: a newly founded community of incomers in a territory
an agreed deal resolving a dispute, as in a divorce or legal case

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a founded community and an agreement that ends a dispute.
